title: Did Dodds, Noone and Goodman use double embouchure?
summary: Hall knew Johnny Dodds but not Jimmie Noone; the pair discuss Benny Goodman's reported new embouchure.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: Did you get through all your questions there? Yes, I think so. If you can think of something else, anything else that you'd like to ask about. I was going to ask much more if you knew for sure if people like Johnny Dodds or Jimmy Noon put their teeth on the instrument too. Do you think you remember? No.
I remember Johnny Dodds. I heard about Jimmy Noon but I never did have a chance to meet Jimmy.
I met him and of course I didn't pay much attention to him.
Well, he was playing a double ember show you call it.
I wondered if he did. I didn't know. No, I don't know. Who's Jimmy Noon?
I didn't either. And Barney, the only one I know.
I think Benny Goodwin is playing a double ember show. Maybe he does. I think so. I can tell the way he put that clapping in his mouth.
He studied with this fellow, Kel, from England, a classical player.

I remember once Louie was complaining when he was supposed to play a concert with him years ago. And he said, you know, all that Benny talked about was this new embouchure. Yeah, embouchure. He was changing over. His new tone he was going to. Yeah. that play solos or parts with the band? Is there any chance of the clarinetist getting too high? I mean, is there any of them you think that's squealing too much up high?
